content:
maria: quick post — ran a small bakeoff on orion-13b weight-only int8 using bitsandbytes vs llm.int8 (on our dedicated gpus). results are...interesting.
kevin: quick numbers pls? :eyes:
maria: short table from the run:
- bitsandbytes (w-only): throughput 520 tok/s, p95 latency 72ms, VRAM 34GB, rouge-l drop +0.6 vs fp16, hallucination rate +1.8% on longform set
- llm.int8: throughput 480 tok/s, p95 latency 83ms, VRAM 30GB, rouge-l drop +0.9 vs fp16, hallucination rate +0.9%
jamie: so bnb faster but noisier quality-wise?
kevin: numbers look close but that hallucination delta on longform is worrying.
maria: exactly. for short prompts (chat style) both are basically indistinguishable. the regression slices are long-context summarization and multi-step instruction following.
sasha: can you paste the invocations/flags you used? want to reproduce.
maria: here — command we used for bitsandbytes path:
```
python serve_bench.py --model orion-13b --quant bnb-8bit-w-only --max-len 1024 --batch 8 --warmup 50 --evalset longform_v2
```
and llm.int8 path:
```
python serve_bench.py --model orion-13b --quant llm.int8-wonly --max-len 1024 --batch 8 --warmup 50 --evalset longform_v2
```
maria: both on same infra: 8xA10G pod, kernel tuned, GPU mem profiler attached.
kevin: do we have token-level logprobs to compare? could be calibration shift.
jamie: got them — average logprob delta (bnb - llm.int8) at generation start = -0.04, widens for later tokens to -0.12 on avg for longform prompts.
sasha: that aligns with higher hallucination. maybe bnb quantization shifts logits more on later positions due to KV-cache interaction.
bench-bot: eval run id 2205551234-orf: rouge-l, rouge-1/2, exact-match, halluc-rate computed. artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/2205551234/
maria: next steps proposed:
1) run a smaller sweep of misc quant params (group size, block size, use fp16 outliers) for bnb to see if we can recover longform stability
2) run targeted diff eval per-sentence to isolate where hallucination spikes
3) test a hybrid profile: llm.int8 for longform routes, bnb for interactive short chat
kevin: +1 on hybrid routing. we can put that in canary with a traffic split 10/90.
jamie: add regression alerts on the longform slice in console — threshold 1% halluc increase or rouge drop >0.5
sasha: do we prefer to fallback to fp16 or llm.int8 as immediate fallback for bnb failures?
maria: fallback to llm.int8 first since cost delta small and we have capacity headroom. fp16 only if both degrade.
kevin: also capture token-by-token KL divergence between outputs to triage further.
maria: logging note: please attach seed/sample ids from this run when you reproduce. i put a quick repro script in the artifacts path above.
jamie: will schedule the parameter sweep tomorrow and kick off canary config change.
bench-bot: canary config update ticket created: #CAN-8421
maria: thanks all. low risk but worth adding rollout guardrails. :thumbsup:
